title: a create on a child row reads canon loaded at facade open, so two facades can still both take one id
body:
**A CREATE ON A CHILD ROW CHECKS CANON THAT WAS LOADED WHEN THE FACADE OPENED, SO TWO FACADES CAN STILL BOTH TAKE ONE ID.**

Filed on vc's word (2026-08-29), stated up front rather than discovered later. `8aebe2ce` closed the single-writer half of hv's 2026-08-28 ruling for criteria and acceptance tests: `ac new` and `at new` now refuse an id the thread already has. **That refusal is a FACADE check, and it inherits the staleness of the read it is made against.**

## Why it could not be closed the way `ccfefe2b` closed the parent case

For threads and issues the refusal is not a check at all -- it is a UNIQUE constraint firing INSIDE the write transaction (`store::Door::Create`). That holds however stale the caller's canon is, because the database is asked at the moment of the write.

**A criterion and an acceptance test are CHILD rows, and `write_thread` replaces a thread's child set wholesale.** There is no per-child UNIQUE key for a create door to fire on, so there is nothing for the store to refuse. The check therefore has to be made before the write, against `self.canon`, which was loaded when the facade opened.

## The window, concretely

Two facades open on one project before either writes. Both read a thread whose criteria do not include `AC-01.1`. Both are told the id is free; both build a thread carrying it; the second `write_thread` replaces the child set the first one wrote. **Both callers are told `created`.** This is 0131's shape one level down -- and unlike 0131 the numbers are caller-assigned, so it needs two people to choose the same id rather than an allocator handing it out twice.

## What is NOT claimed

- **No incident.** This is reasoned from the mechanism, not reproduced. The 0131 race was not characterised either and the property was driven instead of the race.
- **It is not reachable by one operator at a terminal**, which is the whole population the refusal in `8aebe2ce` does close.
- **It is not a regression.** Before `8aebe2ce` the second write also won, and silently. What changed is that the sequential case is now refused, which narrows the window rather than opening one.

## What closing it would take

The thread write has to become CONDITIONAL on the row set it was derived from -- a compare-and-swap on the child set, or a per-child constraint the store can enforce. Either is a change to the write path rather than to the create door, which is why it was deliberately not attempted inside `8aebe2ce`: settling it there would have been a real defect argued into the commit that was closing a different one.

## Cross-references

`0131` is the parent ruling and the store half. `8aebe2ce` carries the child half and states this limit in `Facade::ac_new`'s doc comment and in the header of `a_create_refuses_a_child_id_that_is_taken.rs`, so a reader meeting the refusal finds the boundary next to it rather than assuming the class is closed.
